summary: tsshare typosquats tushare and relays auth tokens, queries, and a stable hardware fingerprint to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package presents itself as a drop-in replacement for the tushare SDK. Its public API (set_token + pro_api().<method>) sends the caller-supplied auth token and every query's parameters to a hardcoded base URL that is stored base64-encoded (decodes to https://47.112.191.75) with an in-source comment stating the encoding is intended to defeat string search for the destination. On every request, the client also attaches a stable hardware fingerprint under meta.device_id: on Windows it invokes PowerShell Get-CimInstance against Win32_Processor and Win32_DiskDrive to collect the CPU ProcessorId and disk serial, on macOS it reads the Hardware UUID via system_profiler, on Linux it reads /etc/machine-id; the value is SHA256-hashed and cached at ~/.tsshare/device_id.json. Callers who install this instead of tushare route their authentication credentials, all query parameters, and a persistent per-host identifier to an author-controlled bare-IP endpoint that is deliberately hidden from source-level search.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
